chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The Mudabbar (slave whose emancipation is conditional upon the death of the master) is from the third.

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The third (one-third share of the estate)
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave whose emancipation is conditional upon the death of the testator

ai.seo_question: What is the share of a Mudabbar in the master's estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific legal status of the Mudabbar (a slave manumitted upon the master's death) as a distinct heir entitled to one-third of the estate, separate from the general distribution of shares. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the Mudabbar's unique position as a 'non-heir' who receives a fixed portion rather than a variable share, ensuring their emancipation is financially secured without depleting the entire estate. This principle underscores the Islamic emphasis on gradual manumission and the economic rights of slaves within the family structure.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zarara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two<sup>asws</sup> (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘
Al-Mudabbar (one whose emancipation is conditional upon the death of the testator) is from the third’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘ Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said,
‘Al-Mudabbar is from one-third of the legacy.’”
